members.name: ArcDelegate
members.doc:
Bindings are owned by a shared block rather than by the delegate
itself so a Broadcast can keep walking after a handler destroys the
delegate (a button whose click closes the panel that owns it). A
copied delegate must not share that block — it would fire the
source's listeners — so copies deep-copy it.

members.name: Add
members.doc: The returned handle is what Remove takes

members.name: Add
members.signature: template<typename T> CDelegateHandle Add(T* obj, Ret (T::*method)(Args...))

members.name: Broadcast
members.doc:
Handlers may add or remove listeners, destroy the widget that owns
this delegate, or close the panel a LATER listener belongs to. The
walk therefore never touches `this` after the first call: it pins
the shared block, snapshots the handles, and before each call
re-resolves the handle against the live list — a listener removed
by an earlier handler is skipped rather than run against an object
that no longer exists. The functor is copied out before the call
because a handler that removes ITSELF would otherwise free the
storage it is executing from.

members.signature: template<typename... Args> static CText Format(const std::string& pattern, Args&&... args)
members.doc:
FText-grade formatting: "{0}", "{name}", "{0}|plural(one=..,other=..)",
"{0}|ordinal(..)", "{0}|select(..)" (see Mowo::FText::FormatArgs).
The pattern and the arguments are kept, not the result, so the text
re-formats when the culture changes: a localized pattern re-resolves,
a CText argument re-resolves, and numbers re-format with the new
culture's separators and digits. Substitution is one pass, so an
argument's own text is never searched for placeholders.

members.name: Widget
members.doc:
Weak on purpose: this manager is a DLL-lifetime static, and the
widgets it snapshots are owned by the host executable. A strong ref
here outlives the host's own statics and the last release lands
after their memory is gone.

members.name: Reset
members.doc:
Drops every widget reference and the cached tree. Ordered shutdown
calls this so nothing survives into static-destructor time.

members.doc: Build the widget tree snapshot (no timing — cheap, one walk).

members.name: ProfileTree
members.doc:
Build the snapshot AND time every subtree's measure pass. Costs
O(widgets * depth) because a container's ComputeDesiredSize
re-measures its whole subtree and AWidget exposes no per-widget
hook — run it on demand, not every frame.

members.name: MeasureFullLayoutMs
members.signature: static float MeasureFullLayoutMs(const TSharedPtr<AWidget>& root, float layoutScale, const CGeometry& geometry)
members.doc:
Times a full from-scratch measure + arrange of an arbitrary tree.
This is the benchmark primitive: it reports what a completely
invalidated layout costs, which is exactly what a desired-size
cache is supposed to remove.

members.name: MeasureOnlyMs
members.signature: static float MeasureOnlyMs(const TSharedPtr<AWidget>& root, float layoutScale)
members.doc:
Times ONLY the measure pass (no arrange), so the desired-size
cache's skip path can be read without ArrangeChildren — which
still runs unconditionally — hiding it.

types.name: ADockSpace::FLiveTearOffHooks
types.doc:
Live tear-off: when Begin is bound and returns true, a drag that
escalates out of its well detaches into a host-owned floating window
immediately; Update/End then follow the same mouse capture. A host
that leaves these unbound keeps the ghost-chip drag with tear-off
deferred to release (OnTabDraggedOut).

floating window stays where it is instead of attempting a drop.

members.name: CacheDesiredSize
members.doc:
Recomputes the desired size only when something can have changed:
this widget or a descendant was invalidated, the layout scale moved,
or a global invalidation epoch fired. Also repairs the parent links
of every enumerable child so Invalidate() has a chain to walk.

members.name: CanCacheDesiredSize
members.doc:
Opt-in for the desired-size cache. A widget may only return true when
every input to its ComputeDesiredSize is either constant or routed
through Invalidate(): bound attributes, measure-reads-arrange feedback,
children generated during arrange, and children that are not reported
by GetChildAt all disqualify it. Default is false, so a widget nobody
audited keeps the previous always-recompute behaviour.

members.name: DesiredSizeDependsOnChildren
members.doc:
False when ComputeDesiredSize never reads a child size — a scroll
box, a list, a tree, a viewport: their measure is a constant and the
widgets under them are measured by their own arrange body instead.
The measure pass then stops here, where before it walked the whole
panel below to hash sizes that could not move this widget.

members.name: GetLayoutRevision
members.doc:
Bumped every time this widget's own inputs are invalidated. Anything
that memoizes a per-widget derived result (a text block's shaped
layout) keys on it instead of re-deriving the key from the inputs.

members.name: GetLayoutEpoch
members.doc:
The global invalidation epoch. A memo built from process-wide state
(the active style set, the font manager) is only valid while this
still matches, because InvalidateAllWidgets is what a style or font
swap announces itself with.

members.name: GetMeasureCount
members.doc:
How many ComputeDesiredSize calls CacheDesiredSize has let through.
The layout tests assert that a second pass over an unchanged tree
computes nothing at all; without a counter the only available
evidence would be a wall-clock delta, which proves nothing on a
loaded machine.

members.name: CanSkipArrange
members.doc:
Opt-in for the arrange skip. A widget may only return true when
ArrangeChildren is a pure function of the allotted geometry, its own
attributes and its children's cached desired sizes — and every input
that can move announces itself through Invalidate(). A body that
clamps a scroll offset, recycles rows, re-elides text against the
width it just handed out, or reads a clock disqualifies the widget:
skipping it would freeze the very thing the body exists to update.

The default answer is "yes" for a widget that reports no children,
because the base ArrangeChildren is empty and there is nothing to
freeze. Every widget that OVERRIDES ArrangeChildren therefore has to
state its own answer; one that stays silent reports children and is
refused by this default.

members.name: GetArrangeCount
SetArrangeSkipEnabled
members.doc:
Kill switch for the arrange skip, so a suspected stale-layout bug can
be confirmed or cleared in one process instead of across two builds.

members.name: OnPaint
members.signature: virtual int32_t OnPaint(const CArcPaintArgs& args, const CGeometry& allottedGeometry, CArcUIRenderer& renderer, int32_t layerId) const = 0

members.name: CanRetainPaint
members.doc:
Opt-in for the retained-paint cache. A widget may only return true
when its OnPaint output is a pure function of the arranged geometry,
its own attributes and its children — and every input that can move
announces itself through InvalidatePaint() (or Invalidate(), which
implies it). A bound attribute the body paints from, a running
animation, a blinking caret, a selection highlight, rows a view
recycles per frame, or a surface re-rendered every frame all
disqualify it: replaying would freeze exactly what the body exists
to update.

The default is false, so a widget nobody audited keeps painting.

members.name: InvalidatePaint
members.doc:
Drops this widget's retained paint and every ancestor slice that
contains it, without touching layout. This is the lighter sibling of
Invalidate(): hover, press, focus, a swatch colour — anything that
changes only what is drawn — belongs here, because invalidating the
layout for it would throw away a measure and an arrange that are
still correct.

The walk runs to the root rather than stopping at the first flagged
ancestor: only the OUTERMOST opted-in widget in a nesting run owns a
slice, so the widgets in between hold nothing to stop at and the
stale slice above them would survive.

members.name: InvalidateAllPaint
members.doc:
Drops every retained slice in the process without walking any tree.
The hammer for changes no widget can observe locally: a style set
swap, reloaded fonts, a font atlas rebuilt under already-baked glyph
UVs, a device pixel density change.

members.name: GetInvalidationSerial
members.doc:
Ticks on every invalidation of any kind anywhere — a layout or paint
walk, a slice dropped, a global drop. The window manager skips a
window's paint only while this has not moved since the window last
painted. Invalidations raised while a paint pass runs count apart:
a widget re-flagging itself mid-paint is judged by what it then
draws, and counting it here would let one window's paint keep every
other window from ever skipping.

members.name: SetInvalidationCensus
members.doc:
Counts, by widget type, the invalidations raised outside a paint pass
while on: the answer to "what keeps this window from skipping".

members.name: NoteLivePaint
members.doc:
A paint that changes with the clock rather than with any write — a
blinking caret, a scroll bar waiting out its hide delay — calls this,
so the window it paints in keeps painting while it lasts.

members.name: BeginObservedCollect
members.doc:
The observed widgets a window's paint marked on screen, gathered so
a frame that skips that paint can keep them on the poll list:
otherwise every bound value in the window stops being polled the
first frame nothing repaints it, and nothing would wake it again.

members.name: KeepObservedOnScreen
members.signature: static void KeepObservedOnScreen(const std::vector<std::weak_ptr<const AWidget>>& widgets)

members.name: GetPaintCount
members.doc:
How many OnPaint bodies ran, and how many were answered from a
retained slice instead. The tests assert that a second pass over an
unchanged tree replays rather than repaints; a wall-clock delta
would prove nothing on a loaded machine.

members.name: SetRetainedPaintEnabled
members.doc:
Kill switch, so a suspected stale-pixel bug can be confirmed or
cleared in one process instead of across two builds.

members.name: CensusRetainedPaint
members.signature: static void CensusRetainedPaint(const TSharedPtr<AWidget>& root, std::vector<std::pair<std::string, FRetainedPaintCensus>>& outByType)

members.name: PollAttributes
members.doc:
Re-evaluates every bound attribute this widget paints or measures
from and invalidates on the ones that moved. Returns whether any is
still bound — false takes the widget off the poll list. A widget
that overrides this may treat its bound attributes as plain values
in CanCacheDesiredSize / CanSkipArrange / CanRetainPaint while
AreBoundAttributesObserved() holds.

members.name: AreBoundAttributesObserved
members.doc:
True once this widget is on the poll list. Registration needs a
shared owner, so a widget built on the stack never observes and
keeps the conservative answers.

members.name: PollObservedAttributes
members.doc:
Runs PollAttributes on every observed widget that was on screen
last frame and drops the rest off the list. Once a frame, before
layout, from the window manager. Returns how many were polled.

Only the ones on screen: a getter belongs to the widget's own
frame, and the shell keeps whole hidden panels and parked popups
alive with their bindings — six hundred of them against no polls at
all was the shape this list had before it pruned itself.

members.name: StopObservingTree
members.doc:
Takes root and everything under it out of the next poll, as if it
had not painted last frame. A window that is closing or loses its
root still has holders (the input processor's hovered path, a
caller's reference) keeping the tree alive for a frame, and its
getters may point into an owner that is already gone — the Project
Settings crash was exactly that poll.

members.name: IsAttributePollDue
members.doc:
Whether the next PollObservedAttributes would run this widget's
getters.

members.name: ObserveAttributes
members.doc:
Puts this widget on the poll list. Called by TAttribute::SetOwner /
Bind through CArcAttributeOwner; a widget that binds its own
attributes without an owner can call it directly.

marks the widget on screen for the next poll and, when a slice is
being recorded around it, writes it into that slice so the replay
can keep marking it. Before every return, or an empty text block
would drop off the poll and its slice would never learn it filled.

members.name: OnDragEnter
members.signature: virtual bool OnDragEnter(const CGeometry& geo, const CDragDropEvent& event)
members.doc:
Drop-target contract. While a drag operation is live the drag-drop
manager resolves the widget under the cursor on every move — the
widget holding mouse capture (the drag source) and its subtree are
skipped — and walks that path leaf to root offering the drag.

OnDragEnter is the offer: return true to become the target, false to
pass it up the path. A widget that declines must leave no state
behind, because it never receives OnDragLeave. The target then gets
OnDragOver on every move (return false to show the rejected cursor
without giving the target up) and exactly one OnDragLeave when the
cursor moves off it or the drag ends. OnDrop lands before that final
leave; returning true reports the drop as consumed.

members.doc:
Focus that arrived from the keyboard (Tab, arrows) rather than a
click — the :focus-visible rule. A ring on every clicked button is
noise; no ring on a tabbed-to button leaves a keyboard user lost.

Pins a pointer or keyboard state for display. Hover and Focused
set the flags the widget already reads; Pressed is reported by
IsPreviewPressed, which the spec-driven widgets OR into their own
press. The pin holds until the widget is hovered, focused or left
for real, so a gallery shows it on a hit-test-invisible row.

members.doc:
Rich tooltip (U1): an arbitrary widget hosted in the tooltip popup
window instead of plain text lines — icons, keycap chips, asset
thumbnails. Takes precedence over SetToolTipText when set.

members.name: GetAccessibleRole
members.doc:
What a screen reader calls this control. Widgets override the role
and value; deriving them from the type name broke for every
subclass and left numeric, radio and multi-line fields unnamed.

members.name: GetAccessibleName
members.doc:

found under the widget (an icon glyph is not text); otherwise the

members.doc: Parent tracking (weak reference to avoid cycles)

members.name: SetRenderTransform
members.doc:
A transform on how this widget paints and is hit, not on its
layout, applied about the pivot (a fraction of its size, the centre
by default). Its parent applies it — containers arrange and paint
their children through ArrangeChildWidget / PaintChildWidget — so
the whole subtree turns with it and hit testing follows. A layout
invalidation, because the transform lives in the arranged geometry
the hit test reads.

members.name: ComputeRenderTransform
members.doc:
The render transform in absolute space for the given layout
geometry: about the pivot point of its rect.

members.signature: static void ArrangeChildWidget(AWidget& child, const CGeometry& childGeometry)
members.doc:
Arranges a child into childGeometry with the child's own render
transform folded into the geometry it caches, so the transform
reaches its hit test and every geometry built below it.

members.signature: static int32_t PaintChildWidget(const AWidget& child, const CArcPaintArgs& args, CArcUIRenderer& renderer, int32_t layerId)
members.doc: Paints a child from its cached geometry under its render transform.

members.name: SetRenderOpacity
members.doc:
The opacity multiplies into every vertex colour the widget emits, so
a slice recorded at one value paints the wrong alpha at another.

members.name: IsTextInput
members.doc:
True for widgets that consume plain keystrokes as text while focused
(editable text boxes and their kin). The input processor suppresses
modifier-less command chords when such a widget has focus.

members.name: ConsumesTab
members.doc:
True only for a widget that types Tab as a character (the multi-line
box). Every other text input lets Tab move focus, which is the only
way out of a single-line field from the keyboard.

members.name: GetFocusVisual
members.doc:
How this widget's keyboard focus is drawn by CArcFocusRing. Text
inputs answer None (their focused border says it); a row-like
widget answers InsetBorder.

members.name: PaintsOwnFocus
members.doc:
True for a widget whose own paint shows keyboard focus where the
framework's ring would be wrong (the ring round a slider's thumb,
a tree's or list's keyboard row): it answers None above and still
shows focus, which the keyboard audit has to know.

members.name: OwnsKeyboard
members.doc:
True while a self-drawn overlay (a command palette) holds the
keyboard the way a modal does: Tab is its own key there, so the
keyboard audit closes it with Escape before tabbing the window.

members.name: GetFocusRadius
members.doc:
The corner radius of the control's own outline. The focus ring is
drawn concentric with it (this plus the gap and stroke), so a pill
toggle gets a pill ring and a 2 px checkbox a near-square one; one
fixed radius made every ring a 4 px rounded box whatever it circled.

members.name: AllowsKeyBubbling
members.doc:
Whether a key this widget declined may be offered to its ancestors.
Overriding to false restores the pre-bubbling behaviour for this
widget and everything under it — the opt-out for a widget tree
(a game HUD arbitrating its own input, say) that must not have its
leftover keys reinterpreted by whatever it happens to be parented
to. The framework fallbacks still run; only the walk stops.

members.name: IsFocusable
members.doc:
Focusability predicate for directional (gamepad/keyboard)
navigation — the FNavigationConfig seam. Interactive widgets
override to true; navigation additionally requires the widget to
be visible and enabled.

members.name: OnActivate
members.doc:
A gamepad/keyboard accept aimed at this widget. Widgets translate
the activation internally (fire the click delegate, toggle, open)
instead of receiving a synthesized mouse click. Returns true when
the activation was consumed.

members.name: Invalidate
members.doc:
Marks this widget's desired size dirty, then walks up the parent chain
flagging ancestors. The walk stops at the first ancestor already
flagged — everything above it was flagged when it was.

members.name: NeedsSubtreeLayout
members.doc: True when this widget or anything below it needs a fresh measure.

members.name: InvalidateAllWidgets
members.doc:
Drops every cached desired size in the process, without walking any
tree. This is the hammer for changes no widget can observe locally:
active style set swapped, fonts reloaded, application scale changed.

members.name: SetFocusScopeId
members.doc:
The focus scope this widget roots, None on everything else. The
command system walks from the focused widget to the root, collects
the scopes named along the way and offers a chord to them innermost
first, before the pushed lists and the global keymap. That is what
makes a shortcut follow the panel the user is in; the editor used to
scope by pointer hover, which retargeted the chord the moment the
mouse drifted off the panel mid-edit. Focus itself is unchanged —
OnFocusReceived/OnFocusLost and CReply::SetUserFocus still own it,
and a scope is only read off the path they produce.

types.name: AWidget::FArrangeScope
types.doc:
Guard every opted-in ArrangeChildren body opens with. It answers
whether the arrange can be skipped, and on destruction — so early
returns are covered — records the geometry this pass ran with and
re-folds the subtree's skippability.
Only the two functions are exported, not the class: dllexporting a
type with a reference member and a by-value CGeometry buys nothing
and costs a C4251 per translation unit that includes this header.

types.name: AWidget::FRetainedPaintCensus
types.doc:
Where retention stands across a tree, per widget type: how many
opted in, how many have given up, how many proved their subtree and
how many hold a slice a clean frame could replay. Read by the
bench, because a low replay count says only that something is
wrong and this says where.

types.name: AWidget::FPaintScope
types.doc:
Guard an opted-in container's OnPaint opens with. It answers whether
the subtree can be replayed and, on destruction — so early returns
are covered — closes the recording and re-folds the subtree.

A leaf needs no scope: its parent's slice already contains it, and
the fold accepts a childless widget on CanRetainPaint() alone. Only
a widget that paints children has to open one, because a container
that opted in without folding would veto every ancestor above it.
Only the functions are exported, not the class: dllexporting a type
with reference members and a by-value CGeometry buys nothing and
costs a C4251 per translation unit that includes this header.

members.name: ArrangeStack
members.signature: void ArrangeStack(const std::vector<float>& cardHeights, float windowHeight, const FToastArea& area, float deltaTime, bool snap)
members.doc:
Lays the cards out bottom-up from the area's corner, oldest lowest,
so a new card never moves the ones already up. cardHeights is one
height per active card. What does not fit between the corner and
area.Top (or past MaxVisible) folds, oldest first, into a "+N more"
line at the bottom: the newest card is always shown. Each card's
StackOffset eases toward its slot over deltaTime; snap places
every card at once (a different window took the stack).

members.name: RenderOwnedWindows
members.doc:
Renders and presents only the Arc-owned swapchain windows, skipping
wrapped/external ones, all on the calling thread. Host engines call
it once per frame after PaintMainWindow. Does not tick the animation
manager — PaintMainWindow already did.

members.name: ProduceOwnedWindows
members.doc:
RenderOwnedWindows in three parts for a host that records on its
own rendering thread. Produce runs on the game thread (layout,
paint, batch snapshot) and pins each window's batch; Record opens
each window's frame, records the pinned batch and closes it; Present
hands each recorded window to its swapchain's deferred present.
Record and Present touch no widget and no platform window, so they
may run on another thread while the game thread produces the next
frame. The windows stay alive until the record fence (below) ran.

members.name: SetRecordFence
members.doc:
Waits until no produced window frame is still being recorded. Run
before any window's GPU side is torn down; a host recording owned
windows on another thread must install it.

members.name: HasOwnedWindowsToRender
members.doc:
True when RenderOwnedWindows would record at least one window. A
host that must fence its render thread before that recording asks
first, so a frame with no floating panel or popup keeps its overlap.

members.name: DismissTooltip
members.doc:
Hides the hover tooltip immediately and keeps it hidden until the
pointer moves again. Every mouse press routes through here, as does
every popup that opens and every loss of window focus.

members.name: SetOSPopupsEnabled
members.doc:
Menus and tooltips as real OS windows (borderless, non-activating,
topmost) so they can overhang the owning window like every native
app. On by default; when off — or when popup creation fails — the
legacy in-window overlay painting takes over.

members.name: SetPopupsInWindowWhenTheyFit
members.doc:
A menu or tooltip that fits inside its owning window paints there,
as Slate does, and only one that must overhang the window gets an
OS window of its own. Each OS popup costs a swapchain, a command
buffer and a renderer, and every one of those once drained the GPU
on the game thread: the owner's 1-19 s stalls sat next to popup
creation and resizes. On by default.

Call this instead of ProcessEvents() when the host polls SDL events itself.

a modal or menu owned it, or the focused widget swallowed it. A

Returns true if the event was RECOGNIZED (translated); pass

types.name: CArcTouchGestureFilter
types.doc:
M4.2 touch feel. Touch pointer events (IsTouch, translated by the SDL
backend from the primary finger) run through a deferred-press state
machine before they reach widget routing:

- finger down forwards NOTHING until the gesture resolves — a
finger wobbles 5-10 px even when the user means a plain tap, and
forwarding raw motion turns every tap into an accidental drag
against the widgets' 4-5 px mouse thresholds;
- lift inside the slop radius = tap: the held-back press and the
release are forwarded back-to-back at the press point;
- motion beyond the slop = drag: the held-back press is forwarded
at the press point, then the motions flow through live;
- holding inside the slop past the delay = long-press: a
right-button click (down+up) is synthesized — the touch idiom for
"context menu" — and the eventual lift is swallowed.

Coordinates are Arc logical units, which are already DPI-normalized,
so the slop is a plain constant. Mouse events pass through untouched.

types.name: CArcMowoBridge
types.doc:
Runs Arc on Mowo's live Vulkan device (shared-device mode): adopts
instance/device/VMA/queue from VulkanContext, wraps the engine's SDL
window (no swapchain — the host owns it), builds pipelines against the
swapchain format via dynamic rendering, loads the 4 Arc shaders from

initializes DPI scale and activates the generated "Mowo Graphite" style

outConsumed answers the different question the host's game-input
gate needs: did the UI actually take this event? A widget that
handled it, a modal or menu that owned it, or a focused text box
that swallowed the keystroke all set it; a widget that is merely
focused or merely hovered does not. Gating gameplay on focus
instead killed every game key while a HUD button kept focus.

members.name: RenderOverlay
members.doc:

command buffer. Must be called inside the swapchain pass — i.e. from

members.name: RecordOverlay
members.doc:
Records the newest painted overlay whose serial is at most
maxSerial. A host that paints frame N+1 while the render thread
still records frame N passes the serial GetOverlayBatchSerial
returned right after painting N, so a record that starts late
never shows the next frame's UI over this frame's scene.

members.name: RenderSecondaryWindows
members.doc:
Renders + presents every Arc-owned secondary window (crash reporter,
tear-off floating panels) on the calling thread. Each owns its own
RHIViewport — swapchain, backbuffer, depth and sync — and runs a
self-contained BeginFrame/record/Present cycle, so it is never
nested inside the host's main command-buffer pass. A host with a
rendering thread splits it instead (CArcWindowManager's
Produce/Record/PresentOwnedWindows) and records after its main
window's EndFrame in the same render-thread job.

members.name: WrapEngineImage
members.doc:
Wraps a Mowo render target (e.g. SceneRenderer::GetFinalImage) as
an Arc texture for AViewport::SetRenderTarget — zero copies, Arc
samples the engine's VkImageView directly. The returned texture
does NOT own the VkImage/VkImageView (only the sampler Arc creates
for it): the caller must keep the engine image alive for as long
as Arc may still sample it — including frames already in flight —
so release the old image (and this wrapper) only after a device
WaitIdle or once its frames have retired. Wrapping is cheap;
re-wrap whenever the engine recreates the render target (resize).
The image must already be in SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL when Arc
draws — the scene renderer's final-pass handoff guarantees that;
no barrier is recorded here.

every cached measure and retained slice, so every open window

types.name: CArcSDFVertex
types.doc:
Extended vertex for the SDF pipelines (every distance-field shape and the
rounded image). Every shape parameter rides in the vertex rather than
in push constants, so consecutive SDF quads with different parameters
— a card, its shadow, its border, a gradient band — batch into one draw.
SDFParams.w selects the shape (see ArcRoundedRect.hlsl).

types.doc: Per-corner radii, clockwise from the top-left.

types.name: FArcBoxStyle
types.doc:
A box drawn as one quad: fill and border share the same edge, so the
fill can never show past the border at fractional DPI and the outer
anti-aliased band is blended once instead of twice.

types.name: FArcShadow
types.doc:
One shadow layer in CSS box-shadow terms: Blur is the blur radius
(sigma = Blur / 2), Spread grows (or, inset, shrinks) the casting box,
Inset casts inwards from the element's edge instead of outwards.

types.name: FArcGradient
types.doc:
A gradient interpolated in OKLab with premultiplied alpha. Linear:
AngleDegrees in CSS terms (0 = towards the top, 90 = towards the right;
the gradient line spans the box at that angle). Radial: Center and
Radius are fractions of the box; a zero radius reaches the farthest
corner. Stops are positions 0..1 along the line, in ascending order.

members.name: CornerRadius
members.doc:
SDFText only (threshold reuses CornerRadius); RoundedRect/RoundedImage
carry their parameters per-vertex so they batch across param changes.

members.name: Bounds
members.doc:
Absolute logical bounds of everything this command draws. It is what
lets the merge pass answer "would moving this draw earlier change any
pixel?" without re-deriving it from the vertices a second time.

members.name: LayerId
members.doc:
The offscreen layer this command draws into; 0 is the frame's own
target. Commands of different layers never merge.

members.name: LateSlot
members.doc:
1 + the index of the late image this command draws, 0 elsewhere. A
late command never merges, so a batch recorded again on a later frame
can still find it and point it at whatever the slot holds by then.

types.name: FArcLayerPass
types.doc:
One offscreen layer of a frame: its commands render into Target before
the frame's own pass resumes, and a composite command in the parent
samples it. Passes are listed innermost first, so a nested layer is
ready before the layer that composites it renders.

types.name: FArcLateImageDraw
types.doc:
A quad whose texture and valid subrect are read when the batch is
recorded, not when it is painted (CArcLateTexture). Its command is
its own, and its vertices carry 0..1 UVs that the record scales.

members.name: Bound
members.doc:
Filled when the batch is first merged: the command's place after the
merge, its unresolved index count and the 0..1 UVs the record scales,
so every later record resolves against the original rather than
against what the previous resolve left behind.

members.name: TextGamma
members.doc:
The text coverage shaping in force when the frame was painted; the
record reads it from here because the next paint may already be
changing the live values on another thread.

members.name: Serial
members.doc:
Stamped per snapshot. Recording the same snapshot again — twice in one
frame under frame generation, or on later frames while its window
skips its paint — reuses the merge and every frame slot's upload.

members.name: Merged
members.doc:
The draw list is merged once; merging an already merged list again
would drop the late commands an unresolved slot zeroed.

members.name: ContentHash
members.doc:
Content hash of what the paint produced, set only when the window
manager asked for one (CArcUIRenderer::SetHashSnapshots).

members.name: HeldTextures
members.doc:
Every texture the commands sample, held for as long as this batch
can still be recorded: a window that skips its paint records the
same batch long after the widget that painted it dropped its image.
HoldsAllTextures is false when one of them is not reference counted
and so cannot be kept alive here — such a batch is never replayed.

members.name: SamplesOnlyStatic
members.doc:
Nothing but the white texel and the glyph atlases, no late image, no
offscreen layer: a window showing such a batch looks the same however
often it is presented, so a skipped paint may skip the present too.

members.name: Observed
members.doc:
The observed widgets whose paint this slice stands in for. A replay
never visits them, so the replaying widget marks them alive from
here — that is what keeps their bound attributes on the poll while
the slice keeps them off the screen walk.

Called with names like "ArcStandard.vert.spv", "ArcStandard.frag.spv", etc.

members.name: SharePipelinesFrom
members.doc:
Takes another renderer's pipelines and white texture instead of
building its own, when both draw to the same colour format. A
pipeline depends on nothing else here, and building four per popup
window plus a white texture whose upload waits on the GPU was most
of what opening a menu or tooltip cost the game thread.

members.name: Shutdown
members.doc:
gpuRetired: the GPU already finished every frame this renderer
recorded, so the idle wait before freeing is skipped.

members.name: ClearDescriptorCache
members.doc: Clear descriptor cache immediately (use WaitIdle first!)

members.name: DeferClearDescriptorCache
members.doc:
Asks for the whole DS cache to be retired before the next record;
the sets are destroyed once every in-flight frame that could
reference them has drained. Safe to call every frame and from any
thread: the cache itself belongs to whichever thread records, so a
paint running beside a record only leaves a request. The old
countdown was re-armed by each call, so callers firing per frame
(thumbnail wraps while browsing) kept the cache from EVER clearing
and pinned evicted thumbnails' GPU images alive.

members.name: GetDescriptorCacheSize
members.doc:
Descriptor sets currently cached for reuse; the deferred clear
only reaches this at the next record.

members.name: SetDynamicRendering
members.doc:
Enable dynamic rendering mode (VK 1.3). Must be called BEFORE CreatePipelines().
Required when the host engine uses vkCmdBeginRendering instead of VkRenderPass.

members.name: Begin
members.signature: void Begin(float width, float height, float pixelDensity = 1.0f)
members.doc:
width/height are LOGICAL units (the space every widget paints in);
pixelDensity maps them onto the physical render target (2.0 on a
Retina drawable). The ortho projection stays logical — only the
hardware scissors convert to device pixels.

members.name: GetPixelDensity
members.doc:
Logical-to-device factor of the current frame. Glyph emission snaps
quads to multiples of 1/density in logical space with it.

members.name: SetFramebufferTarget
members.doc:
The batch is recorded into an engine framebuffer pass rather than
the swapchain pass. On the backends whose framebuffer passes map
clip space y-up (IArcRHIDevice::FramebufferPassesFlipY) the
projection flips so the target is not upside down.

members.name: MergeDrawCommands
members.doc:
Collapses the recorded draw list in place and returns the number of
commands left. A command joins an earlier one that shares its
pipeline, texture, distance-field parameters and an effective clip
when nothing drawn between the two overlaps it — moving it earlier
then cannot change a pixel, which is what keeps painter's order
intact while the alternation between rounded rects and text stops
costing a draw call each. Pure and device-free, so the batching
rules are testable without a GPU.

members.name: SnapshotPendingBatch
members.doc:
The paint/record handoff is double-buffered: a snapshot publishes
into the slot that does NOT hold the newest batch, so the game
thread can paint frame N+1 while the render thread still records
frame N out of the other slot. The record takes the newest published
batch whose serial is at most maxSerial — a host that paints ahead
passes the serial it painted for that frame, so a late record never
picks up the next frame's UI. The host keeps at most one snapshot
ahead of the record still running (the editor's frame fence).

members.name: GetPublishedBatchSerial
members.doc:
Serial of the newest snapshot published to the record side, 0
before the first one.

members.name: GetLastRecordedSerial
members.doc: Serial of the batch the last record drew (render-thread side).

members.name: BeginRetainedRecord
members.doc:
Opens a retained-paint recording. Everything emitted until the
matching EndRetainedRecord is captured into the slice. Returns false
when the recording cannot start — a recording is already open (only
the outermost opted-in widget in a nesting run owns a slice) or a
transform is active, which would bake into the vertices.

members.name: EndRetainedRecord
members.signature: bool EndRetainedRecord(FArcRetainedSlice& slice, const ArcVec2& origin)
members.doc:
Closes the recording and copies the emitted range into the slice,
rebased to origin. Returns false — and leaves the slice invalid —
when the body did something the replay cannot reproduce: it pushed a
clip or a transform of its own, or left the clip stack unbalanced.

members.name: AbortRetainedRecord
CanReplayRetained
members.doc:
Whether the state the slice was recorded under is still in force.
The clip is compared for equality rather than translated: a slice
carries the ambient clip on every one of its commands, and a clip
that moved is a clip whose commands would have to be rebuilt.

members.name: ReplayRetained
members.signature: void ReplayRetained(const FArcRetainedSlice& slice, const ArcVec2& translation)
members.doc:
Appends the slice's geometry and commands in recorded order, moved
by translation. Command bounds move with it so the merge pass's
overlap rule still sees where the geometry really lands.

members.name: NoteObservedWidget
members.doc:
An observed widget painted while a recording is open. Recorded into
the slice, so the replay can keep it alive for the attribute poll.

members.name: DrawPolyline
members.signature: void DrawPolyline(const ArcVec2* points, uint32_t count, const ArcColor& color, float thickness, bool closed = false)
members.doc:
An anti-aliased polyline: each segment is one distance-field quad,
and the bisector at every joint hands each pixel to exactly one of
the two segments meeting there, so a translucent line is not
darker at its joints. Round caps and joins.

members.name: SnapRectToPixels

members.doc:
Device-pixel snapping of a logical rect: a span thinner than three
device pixels keeps a whole-pixel width (a 1 px hairline is one
device row wherever it lands), a wider one rounds both edges so
neighbours still tile without a seam.

members.name: ForceSDFEmission
members.doc:
Emits the distance-field geometry even without the SDF pipelines,
so device-free tools and tests can read what the GPU would draw.

members.name: DrawLateImage
members.signature: void DrawLateImage(const ArcRect& rect, const std::shared_ptr<CArcLateTexture>& late, const ArcColor& tint = ArcColor::White)
members.doc:
An image whose texture and valid subrect (CArcLateTexture) are
resolved when the batch is recorded. The quad samples 0..uvMax of
whatever the slot holds then; nothing is drawn if it holds nothing.
Inside a retained recording the slot is read now instead, because
a replay cannot carry the deferred lookup.

members.name: DrawGlyphQuads
members.signature: void DrawGlyphQuads(const ArcVec2& origin, IArcRHITexture* fontAtlas, const CArcGlyphQuad* quads, uint32_t quadCount, const ArcColor& color, float offsetX)
members.doc:
There is deliberately no per-glyph text entry point: every string goes
through CArcTextLayoutCache (DrawString or Paint), because the
hand-rolled loops it replaced decoded UTF-8 byte by byte, bypassed the
fallback chain and drew mojibake for anything outside Latin-1.
Bulk glyph path: quads carry their own size, so no intermediate
position/UV arrays are built and the vertex/index buffers grow once
per run instead of once per glyph.

screen from origin (top-left of the vertical column, columnWidth =
the layout's line height). Vertical sidebar tabs.

members.name: ClipConvexPolygon
members.signature: static int ClipConvexPolygon(const ArcVec2* subject, int subjectCount, const ArcVec2* clip, int clipCount, ArcVec2* out, int maxOut)
members.doc:
Convex-polygon clipping for rotated clip rects. Both are pure and
device-free so tools and tests can reason about a rotated clip without
a live renderer. ClipConvexPolygon is Sutherland-Hodgman and needs out
capacity for at least subjectCount + clipCount vertices; it returns the
clipped vertex count (0 when the subject is fully outside). The clip
polygon may be wound either way — it is oriented internally. Point tests
treat the boundary (within epsilon) as inside.

members.name: PushLayer
members.doc:
Vertex-alpha opacity: every vertex emitted until PopLayer is faded.
Cheap, but overlapping children show through each other — use an
offscreen layer where that matters.

members.name: PushOffscreenLayer
members.signature: bool PushOffscreenLayer(const ArcRect& bounds, float opacity, const FArcCornerRadii& radii = FArcCornerRadii(), const void* persistentKey = nullptr)
members.doc:
Starts an offscreen layer over bounds: everything drawn until
PopOffscreenLayer renders into a target of its own, which the pop
composites back as one image — real group opacity (two overlapping
children at 50 % do not show a darker overlap) and, with radii,
clipping to a rounded box. A persistentKey keeps the target across
frames for DrawPersistentLayer. Returns false and changes nothing
when a layer cannot be opened here (no device support, an active
transform or rotated clip, an open retained record); the caller
then falls back to PushLayer / PushClipRect.

members.name: DrawPersistentLayer
members.signature: bool DrawPersistentLayer(const void* persistentKey, const ArcRect& bounds, float opacity, const FArcCornerRadii& radii = FArcCornerRadii())
members.doc:
Composites the image a persistent layer rendered on an earlier
frame without rendering its content again — the RetainerBox phase
throttle. False when there is no image for these bounds yet.

members.name: ForceOffscreenLayers
members.doc:
Records layers without device targets, so device-free tests can
read the command partition and the composite a frame would draw.

members.name: GetFrameNumber
members.doc: How many frames this renderer has begun.

members.name: PushTransform
members.doc:
2D affine transform stack. Every vertex emitted between a push and its
matching pop is transformed on the CPU as it is written, so all four
pipelines (unified, both SDF rects and SDF text) rotate identically —
the SDF fragment shaders evaluate their distance from the interpolated
TexCoord, which is affine-invariant, so rounded corners and glyph edges
follow the rotation instead of staying screen-aligned. A clip rect
pushed under a transform keeps an axis-aligned scissor as a coarse bound
but also stores the rotated clip polygon; emitted geometry under a
rotated clip is culled on the CPU against that polygon's real edges, so
a rotated widget is clipped along the parent's turned edges, not a
looser AABB. Unrotated clips stay on the fast scissor-only path.

members.name: PushRotation
members.signature: void PushRotation(float radians, const ArcVec2& pivot)

members.name: PushFloatingText
members.doc:

CArcTextContrast (a popover's surface); they nest.

members.name: GetAtlasRebuildsSeen

types.name: EArcTextDirection
types.doc:
A paragraph's base direction. Auto is UAX #9's P2/P3: the first strong
character outside an isolate decides, and a paragraph with none is LTR.

types.name: CArcBidi
types.doc:
The Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX #9) over one paragraph of
codepoints: explicit embeddings, overrides and isolates (X1-X10), weak and
neutral resolution including bracket pairs (W1-W7, N0-N2), implicit
levels (I1-I2), the paragraph half of L1, and line reordering (L2).
HarfBuzz shapes a run in a direction it is given; this is what decides
the direction and the run boundaries, which Arc used to hard-wire to LTR.

Written in-tree rather than vendored: the property data is a compact range
table of the classes that matter for layout (every RTL script block, the
numerals, the separators and terminators, the explicit formatting
characters, the marks of the scripts that sit beside RTL text), with
unlisted codepoints taking their block's default. ValidateTables pins that
the tables stay sorted, which the binary search depends on.

members.name: NeedsResolution
members.signature: static bool NeedsResolution(const uint32_t* codepoints, size_t count)
members.doc:
Whether the paragraph needs the algorithm at all: true when anything
in it is right-to-left or an explicit right-to-left control. A
paragraph that is all left-to-right resolves to level 0 throughout and
the layout skips the work.

members.name: ParagraphLevel
members.signature: static uint8_t ParagraphLevel(const uint32_t* codepoints, size_t count, EArcTextDirection direction)

members.name: ResolveLevels
members.signature: static void ResolveLevels(const uint32_t* codepoints, size_t count, uint8_t paragraphLevel, std::vector<uint8_t>& outLevels)
members.doc:
One level per codepoint. Characters X9 removes (embedding controls,
boundary neutrals) take the level of the character before them, so a
caller can reorder glyph runs without special-casing them.

members.name: ReorderLine
members.signature: static void ReorderLine(const uint8_t* levels, size_t count, std::vector<uint32_t>& outVisualToLogical)
members.doc:
L2 over one line: outVisualToLogical[v] is the logical index drawn at
visual position v. Trailing whitespace is the caller's to reset to the
paragraph level first (the line half of L1), since only it knows where
the line ends.

members.name: SUBPIXEL_BUCKETS
members.doc:
Horizontal subpixel raster variants for the bitmap atlas: bucket b
rasterizes the outline shifted right by b/SUBPIXEL_BUCKETS of a
device pixel, so a quad snapped to the device grid still lands the
stems where the fractional pen position wanted them. Distance-field
modes ignore the bucket (linear interpolation covers it). Quarters,
as the export's browser places text: halves left a tenth more of
the menu bar's pixels off the reference.

members.name: GetGlyph
members.signature: const CArcGlyphInfo& GetGlyph(FT_Face face, uint32_t codepoint, float fontSize, uint32_t subpixelBucket = 0, float rasterScale = 0.0f)
members.doc:
Get glyph info (rasterizes on-demand if not cached). rasterScale
selects the device-pixel grid the bitmap glyph rasterizes for:
<= 0 uses the atlas-wide supersample (the main window's scale), a
positive value keys a per-scale variant so windows on differently
scaled monitors each get correctly rastered glyphs from one atlas.

members.name: GetGlyphByIndex
members.signature: const CArcGlyphInfo& GetGlyphByIndex(FT_Face face, uint32_t glyphIndex, float fontSize, uint32_t subpixelBucket = 0, float rasterScale = 0.0f)

members.name: WasRebuilt
members.doc: Check if atlas was rebuilt this frame (texture changed, need to rebind)

members.name: GetGeneration
members.doc:
Bumped only when cached UVs stop being valid: the atlas grew, was
flushed after filling up, or changed its raster factor. Adding a glyph
does NOT bump it — the glyph lands in free space and every UV already
handed out still points at the same texels — because the renderer
drops every retained paint slice and descriptor set on a bump, and a
bump per new glyph made typing or scrolling a log repaint the shell.
A bitmap atlas folds its colour companion's rebuilds in: the glyph
UVs every cache keys on this come from both textures.

members.name: GetColorAtlas
members.doc:
Where a bitmap atlas puts colour glyphs (emoji): an RGBA8 atlas of
its own, so the coverage atlas holds one byte per texel instead of
four. Null for the other modes. A glyph with CArcGlyphInfo::Color
has UVs into this atlas's texture.

members.name: CoverageAt
members.signature: uint8_t CoverageAt(uint32_t x, uint32_t y) const
members.doc:
The coverage (or, in a colour atlas, the alpha) of one texel of the
CPU copy; 0 outside it.

members.name: AdvanceFrame
members.doc:
Frame boundary, called once per renderer Begin. Textures the atlas
replaced mid-frame stay alive here until the command lists that may
still sample them have retired, and a full atlas is flushed (emptied
and re-rasterized on demand) here rather than in the middle of a walk
that already resolved UVs against it.

members.name: IsFlushPending
members.doc:
Set when a glyph did not fit and the atlas is already at its maximum
size. The glyph is missing for the rest of this frame only.

members.name: SetMaxAtlasSize
members.doc: Upper bound for growth by doubling; past it the atlas flushes.

members.name: GetRetiredTextureCount
members.doc: Superseded textures still alive because a recorded frame may sample them.

members.name: SetSupersample
members.doc:
High-DPI text: rasterize bitmap glyphs at factor× the requested
size while reporting 1× metrics — the logical-space renderer then
samples them down and text stays crisp on Retina. No effect on
the distance-field modes (already resolution-independent).
Changing the factor drops every cached glyph.

members.name: HasWhiteTexel
members.doc:
A reserved block of opaque white inside the atlas. Untextured UI
quads sample it instead of a separate 1x1 texture, so solid geometry
and text share one descriptor and stay in one batch.

members.name: GetPixelData
members.doc:
The CPU copy the texture is uploaded from. With no device (Initialize
given nullptr) this is the whole atlas: glyphs pack and rasterize the
same way, which is what an offline bake or a headless test needs.

members.name: ValidateWhiteTexel
members.doc:
Reads back the texel the UV resolves to. Solid UI geometry is only
correct while this is opaque white, so it is worth asserting rather
than trusting the packer.

members.name: FlushIfDirty
members.doc: Flush pending pixel data to GPU (call once per frame, after all GetGlyph calls)

members.name: GetPixelBytes
members.doc:
Bytes the CPU-side atlas currently holds. Mirrors the GPU texture
exactly, so it doubles as the memory figure for the mode.

members.name: GetGlyphRenderScale
members.signature: float GetGlyphRenderScale(float fontSize, float rasterScale = 0.0f) const
members.doc:
Drawn pixels per atlas pixel at a given font size. Distance-field
modes rasterize at a fixed size and scale down, so a caller that
sizes a quad from UV extents has to fold this in. rasterScale must
match what the glyphs were fetched with (<= 0 = supersample).

members.name: GetPackedRows
members.doc:
Rows the shelf packer has consumed. Distance-field glyphs are packed
at their render size, not the drawn size, so this is what decides
when the atlas has to double.

members.name: GetRasterizedGlyphCount
members.doc: Rasterization cost so far.

members.name: MIN_RASTER_SCALE
members.doc:
The lowest device grid glyphs rasterize for: UI scale bottoms out at
0.25, and nothing below it is legible anyway.

types.name: EArcFontHinting
types.doc:
How a face's outlines are grid-fitted. Light snaps vertically only and is
the regime for text; None leaves the outline alone, which an icon font
wants because the autohinter bends pictograms as if they were letters.
Mono hints fully to the pixel grid and rasterizes one bit per pixel with
no subpixel shift: a pixel-art font drawn at its design size keeps hard
edges instead of the grey fringes antialiasing smears across them.

members.name: LoadFromMemory
members.signature: bool LoadFromMemory(const uint8_t* data, size_t size)

members.name: FromFace
members.doc:
The CArcFont that owns a FreeType face, or null. The atlas works on
faces, and reads the per-font render settings below through this.

members.name: IsColorFont
members.doc: A face that paints its own colours (COLR, CBDT or sbix): an emoji face.

members.name: SetSyntheticEmbolden
members.doc:
Synthetic weight for a weight the family does not ship (Geist Medium):
the outline is widened by this fraction of the em before rasterizing.

members.name: STEM_DARKEN_FULL_PX
members.doc:
Stem darkening for small text, the way browsers and macOS render it:
an unhinted outline is widened by this fraction of the em at small
device sizes, fading to nothing between STEM_DARKEN_FULL_PX and
STEM_DARKEN_NONE_PX, where the stems are wide enough on their own.
The advances are untouched, so layout does not move.

members.name: SetSyntheticOblique
members.doc:
Synthetic italic for a family with no italic face: x += skew * y.
0.2 is about 11 degrees, the slant most sans italics use.

members.name: SetAbsoluteStroke
members.doc:
A stroke-built icon font drawn at a fixed stroke whatever its size
(Lucide's absoluteStrokeWidth): designStrokeEm is the stroke the
outlines carry as a fraction of the em, strokePx the logical stroke
wanted. Lucide is 2/24 of the em, so at 12 px it is 1 px, at 16 px
1.33 px; the design draws 1.5 px at every size.

members.name: SetPlainCoverage
members.doc:
Glyphs that stand for drawings rather than letters (Lucide): the
design export draws them as SVG paths, which the browser blends
with plain coverage, not through its text gamma. Their quads skip
CArcTextContrast; shaped like text, light icons read heavy and dark
ones thin.

members.name: OutlineDeltaPixels
members.signature: float OutlineDeltaPixels(float devicePixelSize, float rasterScale) const
members.doc:
Device pixels to widen (or thin) every stroke by at a device pixel
size on a raster grid: synthetic weight plus the absolute-stroke
correction. 0 when the font asks for neither.

members.name: GetGlyphIndex
members.doc: FreeType char->glyph lookup, cached (fallback-chain probing is hot)

members.name: GetVerticalMetrics
members.signature: void GetVerticalMetrics(uint32_t pixelSize, int32_t& outAscent, int32_t& outDescent) const
members.doc:
Whole device pixels above and below the baseline at a pixel size:
the OS/2 win metrics when the face has them (they bound every glyph
the font draws, accented capitals and stacked marks included), else
hhea. Rounded outwards, so ink never leaves the box they describe.

members.name: GetInkBounds
members.signature: bool GetInkBounds(uint32_t codepoint, float& outXMin, float& outYMin, float& outXMax, float& outYMax) const
members.doc:
The outline's ink of one glyph in em units, y up from the baseline:
what a centred icon is centred on. False for a glyph the face lacks.

members.name: GetCapHeightEm
members.doc:
Capital height in em units (OS/2 sCapHeight, else the ink of 'H'):
the band a centred label is centred on, so a descender does not
pull it up and the line box's descent does not push it down.

members.name: GetFont
members.signature: CArcFont* GetFont(const std::string& family, bool bold = false, bool italic = false) const

members.name: AddFallbackFont
members.signature: void AddFallbackFont(const Ref<CArcFont>& font, const std::string& language = std::string())
members.doc:
Composite-font fallback chain: fonts probed in order when the
primary face has no glyph for a codepoint (CJK, emoji, symbols).
language tags the face for the Han characters several CJK languages
share ("zh-Hans", "zh-Hant", "ja", "ko"): with the text language set
to one of them, its face is tried first for Han, so Simplified
Chinese stops being drawn with Japanese glyph forms.

members.name: ResolveFontForCodepoint
members.signature: CArcFont* ResolveFontForCodepoint(CArcFont* primary, uint32_t codepoint) const
members.doc:
Resolve the face that carries a codepoint: primary, then the
fallback chain. Returns nullptr when no registered face has it (tofu).

members.name: ResolveFontForCluster
members.signature: CArcFont* ResolveFontForCluster(CArcFont* primary, const uint32_t* codepoints, size_t count) const
members.doc:
Resolve the face for a whole grapheme cluster, so every codepoint of
it shapes in one run: a ZWJ family, a keycap, a flag or a letter with
its marks. Picking per codepoint split "family" into three emoji and
a ZWJ from a text face that never ligated. Emoji presentation (VS16,
ZWJ, regional indicators, keycaps, pictographs) tries colour faces
first; Han tries the text language's tagged face first; then the
first face covering every non-ignorable codepoint; then the base.

members.name: SetTextLanguage
members.doc:
The language of the text being laid out (BCP 47: "en", "zh-CN",
"sr-Cyrl"). Picks the Han face, and tells HarfBuzz which localized
forms to use (Serbian Cyrillic, Turkish i, Romanian s-comma). The
localization manager's culture switch sets it. Changing it drops
every cached layout.

members.name: GetKerning
members.signature: float GetKerning(CArcFont* font, float fontSize, float rasterScale, uint32_t leftGlyphIndex, uint32_t rightGlyphIndex)
members.doc:
Kerning between two glyph indices of the same face at a pixel size,
cached. Legacy (arc.Shaping=0) path only — returns 0 for faces
without a kern table; the shaped path gets GPOS kerning from
HarfBuzz instead.

members.name: SetTextRasterScale
members.doc:
The device-pixel grid text is currently laid out for. The renderer
publishes its window's pixel density here before arranging and
painting, so shaping, kerning and rasterization all describe the
same outlines: advances hinted at the logical size land off the
device grid on any fractional scale, and the glyph bitmaps they
position were hinted at the device size. Layouts are cached per
value, so a second window on a differently scaled monitor keeps its
own set instead of thrashing this one.

members.name: DeviceFontSize
members.signature: static float DeviceFontSize(float logicalSize, float rasterScale)
members.doc: The integer FreeType pixel size a logical size maps to on that grid.

members.name: QuantizeToDeviceGrid
members.signature: static float QuantizeToDeviceGrid(float logicalValue, float rasterScale)
members.doc: Rounds a logical measurement onto whole device pixels.

members.name: AdvanceAtlasFrame
members.doc: Frame boundary for every atlas (see CArcFontAtlas::AdvanceFrame).

members.name: ICON_STROKE_PX
members.doc:
The design's icon rendering (Lucide at 12/14/16 px with an absolute
1.5 px stroke, unhinted). One definition, used by the bridge and by
the row that measures the strokes.

members.name: TEXT_STEM_DARKEN_EM
members.doc:
The design's text rendering, matched to the export's browser
captures: unhinted outlines (advances and stems at their true
fractional positions) with TEXT_STEM_DARKEN_EM of stem darkening
below 14 device px, then the browser's luminance blend
(CArcTextContrast). Fitted pixel by pixel to the menu bar of all
three themes' references: 0.025 em with the old contrast curve put
1.23x the reference's ink into the light theme; 0.01 em with the
gamma blend lands every theme within 2 %.

members.signature: static void ConfigureTextFont(CArcFont& font, float stemDarkeningEm = TEXT_STEM_DARKEN_EM)

The atlas the ordinary text path paints from: the bitmap atlas. The
multi-channel distance-field path was removed — it read worse at the
10-13 px sizes the UI actually uses.

members.doc: The text atlas's colour companion (emoji), or null before Initialize.

members.signature: static void SetFloating(float gamma, float contrast)

members.signature: static float Apply(float coverage, const ArcColor& textColor, bool floating = false)

members.name: COVERAGE_UV_OFFSET
members.doc:
The text UVs the shader recognises: glyph quads from the bitmap atlas
are emitted with U shifted into these bands, which is how one pipeline
tells coverage (reshape, filter under a transform) from an image or a
solid quad without a vertex-format change.

members.name: PLAIN_COVERAGE_UV_SHIFT
members.doc:
Added to either band for a glyph drawn with plain coverage
(CArcFont::HasPlainCoverage): -48 and -64.

members.name: FLOATING_COVERAGE_UV_SHIFT
members.doc:
Added to either band for a text glyph inside a floating surface
(CArcUIRenderer::PushFloatingText): -80 and -96. Icons keep plain
coverage there, so the two shifts never combine.

members.name: AtlasU
members.doc: The atlas U a glyph vertex's banded U stands for.

members.name: DEFAULT_GAMMA
members.doc:
Fitted to the references with TEXT_STEM_DARKEN_EM: the menu bar's
ink against the reference is 1.00x dark, 1.01x light, 1.02x high
contrast (the curve it replaces: 1.01x, 1.23x, 0.96x).

members.name: DEFAULT_FLOATING_GAMMA
members.doc:
Text inside a floating surface (a popover, a confirm): the export's
browser draws those on their own layer with less of the gamma lift.
With the window's pair, editor-mod-mode's confirm and
editor-mcp-indicator's popover carried 1.08-1.25x the reference's
ink in light text and 0.88-0.92x in dark text, where the menu bar
under the same colours measured 1.02x.

members.name: LineHeight
members.doc:
Logical pixels from one baseline to the next; 0 takes the face's own
ascent plus descent. A taller value splits the extra evenly above and
below the glyphs (CSS half-leading), so the text stays centred in its
line. The design tokens' lineHeight lands here.

members.name: LetterSpacing
members.doc:
Logical pixels added after every glyph that advances (the tokens'
letterSpacing; Overline uses 1).

members.name: Features
members.doc:
OpenType features for the shaper, comma or space separated in
HarfBuzz syntax: "tnum" (tabular figures, for numeric columns and
timers that must not jitter), "ss01", "case", "-liga". The tokens'
`features` land here.

types.name: CArcLineBreak
types.doc:
Line-break opportunities per the Unicode Line Breaking Algorithm
(UAX #14), rules LB4 through LB31 over a compact class table. The wrap
used to break only after a space or around a hard-coded CJK range, so it
split "(word" from its bracket, pushed a lone "%" or "。" onto the next
line, and broke between a number and its unit.

Not tailored: Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar (class SA) resolve to AL as
LB1 prescribes for an implementation without a dictionary, so those
scripts still break only at spaces and other explicit opportunities.

None (the start of the text is not a break).

members.name: LineIndexForByte
members.signature: int32_t LineIndexForByte(uint32_t byteOffset, EArcCaretAffinity affinity = EArcCaretAffinity::Downstream) const
members.doc:
Caret/hit-test helpers - byte offsets are into the SOURCE string.

At a soft wrap one byte offset is both the end of a line and the
start of the next, so the offset alone cannot say where the caret
is. The affinity says: Downstream (the default) puts it at the start
of the later line — Home, a click at the left edge, typing — and
Upstream at the end of the earlier one — End, a click past the end.
Resolving every such offset to the earlier line drew the caret after
Home at the end of the line above.

members.name: ShapeRun
members.signature: bool ShapeRun(CArcFont* font, float fontSize, float rasterScale, const char* text, uint32_t textLength, uint32_t runOffset, uint32_t runLength, bool kerning, std::vector<CArcShapedRunGlyph>& outGlyphs, bool rightToLeft = false, const char* features = nullptr)
members.doc:
Shapes at the device pixel size fontSize maps to under rasterScale
and converts the result back to logical units, so every advance and
offset is a whole number of device pixels. Hinted advances taken at
the logical size instead describe a grid-fitting the atlas bitmaps
were never drawn with, and the pen drifts off the pixel grid.

A right-to-left run comes back in HarfBuzz's visual order (clusters
descending), with mirrored brackets and the script's RTL forms; the
caller decides the direction from the run's bidi level.

features is a comma or space separated list in HarfBuzz syntax
("tnum", "ss01", "-liga"); an unparsable entry is skipped.

members.name: GlyphLoadFlags
members.doc:
The FreeType load flags both the shaper (advances) and the bitmap
atlas (outlines) use, so advances and the bitmaps they position come
from one grid-fitting: light hinting, vertical snapping only, unless
the font opted out of hinting altogether (an icon font).

members.name: IsSrgbDisplay
members.doc:
How the NUMBERS are shown and parsed — the stored colour never
changes. Engine colours (light tint, base colour) are LINEAR, so
their raw 0..255 reads much darker than the same colour in any
other tool; sRGB mode gamma-encodes the hex and the R/G/B labels
so a value can be copied in and out of one. Process-wide, like the
saved palette: switching it in one picker switches it everywhere.
Linear (raw) is the default — that is what every picker showed
before the toggle existed.

types.name: ANumericFieldText
types.doc:
The part of a numeric field that cannot be replayed: the value text,
the selection highlight and the caret. It is a leaf the field owns and
arranges over its own rect, hit-test invisible so every press still
lands on the field, and it refuses retained paint only while it has
something moving to show — a caret, a scrubbed value, a run of digits
wider than the frame that needs a clip. Idle, it is as replayable as
any text block, which is what lets the frame around it retain at all.

types.name: ARetainerBox
types.doc:
A retainer: it renders its child subtree into an offscreen layer and
composites that image once, so the group opacity applies to the subtree
as a whole rather than to each child in turn. With a phase count above
one the image persists between frames: the subtree is painted only on
the frames its phase owns, and every other frame redraws the kept image
without walking the subtree. Without layer support (no device, a
transformed ancestor) it falls back to per-child opacity and paints
every frame.

types.name: CWrapSlot

Slot for the wrap panel: only the base padding and alignment apply — a
child's position comes from the flow, not an explicit index.

types.name: AWrapPanel
types.doc:
A flow panel: children are placed along the main axis and wrap to the next
line once the running extent would overflow the panel. Horizontal by
default (rows of children); vertical flows into columns instead. Item
spacing sits between children on a line, line spacing between lines.

members.name: AnimateTo
members.doc:
Retargets toward `target` from wherever the content is drawn now
(`visibleOffset`). Consecutive notches accumulate on the target, so
a fast spin travels the full distance instead of restarting short.

members.name: Fling
members.signature: void Fling(float visibleOffset, float velocity, float minOffset, float maxOffset)
members.doc:
A released drag carries on at `velocity` (content px per second)
and decelerates to rest. The distance is chosen so the curve's
starting speed equals the release speed: no kick, no stall.

members.name: Resolve
members.signature: bool Resolve(float& inOutOffset, float minOffset, float maxOffset)
members.doc:
Writes the offset this frame should lay out at, clamped to the range
the owner can scroll now (content may have shrunk mid-animation),
and returns true; false (offset untouched) when idle. Called from
the owner's arrange, once per frame.

members.name: GetTarget
members.doc: Where the animation will land. Callers stack wheel notches on this.

members.name: SetSmoothScrollEnabled
members.doc:
Process-wide switch (the editor exposes it as a preference); off
makes every wheel notch a jump, as before.

members.name: FLING_SECONDS
members.doc: Duration of a fling's deceleration.

members.name: FLING_MIN_VELOCITY
members.doc: Below this release speed a drag just stops.

members.name: GetReleaseVelocity
members.doc:
The velocity a release at `nowSeconds` should fling with: zero when
the pointer has been still for a beat, because a drag that stopped
before letting go must not take off.

members.doc:
Absolute track rect plus the sizes that set the thumb. Widen the rect
past the painted bar: it is the band that answers the mouse, and a
4 px thumb is not something anyone can hit.

members.name: IsEngaged
members.doc:
True while the user is driving the bar — the owner must keep pointer
capture and must not treat moves as anything else.

members.name: IsHighlighted
members.doc: True when the thumb should paint in its hovered/pressed colour.

members.name: OnPressed
members.doc:
True when the bar took the press. The owner must not also treat the
point as a click on the row underneath.

members.name: OnMoved
members.doc: True when the bar consumed the move (a drag, or a held track press).

members.name: GetCursorAt
members.doc:
The grab cursor over the thumb and while it is dragged, Default
elsewhere — for the owner's OnCursorQuery.

members.name: Advance
members.doc: Runs the hold-to-repeat page timer; feed it the frame delta.

members.name: MIN_THUMB_SIZE
members.doc:
A thumb shorter than this cannot be grabbed, so its length is clamped
and its travel derived from the clamped value.
